articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $1.6M+ philanthropic push creates lasting change for 20,000+ kids across heartlands
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have put more than $1.6 million into a major youth-focused partnership, while their wider foundation work has reached
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have put more than $1.6 million into a major youth-focused partnership, while their wider foundation work has reached more than 20,000 students through its reading program. The couple’s 15 and the Mahomies Foundation has backed projects in Kansas City and Texas, including a $1.625 million commitment to Boys & Girls Clubs of America and a $1 million inclusive playground in Kansas City. Their work also includes literacy, youth sports, food support and grants to local charities. For Mahomes, the focus on children has a personal link, especially through Brittany’s experience with youth clubs growing up.What inspired Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ focus on childrenPatrick Mahomes founded the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation in 2019 with a focus on improving children’s lives through health, wellness, education and support for communities that need resources. Over the years, Brittany Mahomes has also become closely involved in the foundation’s work.One of the biggest steps came in October 2023, when the foundation announced a multi-year partnership with Boys & Girls Clubs of America. The commitment included $1.625 million in funding for clubs in communities connected to the Mahomes family, including Greater Kansas City, Lubbock, Tyler and Whitehouse, Texas. The foundation also pledged $1,500 for every touchdown Mahomes scored during each regular NFL season.The connection was especially personal for Brittany, who used Boys & Girls Club resources when she was younger. Patrick explained why that mattered when the partnership was announced.“We are truly excited to partner with Boys & Girls Clubs of America by investing in the future of children,” Mahomes said. “Kids who attend a Club, like Brittany once did, are provided with the necessary tools and resources to help this generation not only thrive but lead with compassion and purpose.”The money was meant to support improvements at Boys & Girls Club facilities and expand opportunities for young people. In late 2024, clubs in Greater Kansas City and Lubbock also renamed facilities in recognition of the foundation’s support, while a Boys & Girls Clubs of East Texas/The Mentoring Alliance site was set to provide scholarships for up to 300 young people each year.How has the foundation helped students through readingThe partnership is not the only part of the foundation’s work. Its Read for 15 program has become one of its most visible education efforts. The initiative encourages students to read for at least 15 minutes a day for 15 weeks. More than 20,000 students have taken the challenge, according to a 2025 update from Lead to Read KC. Earlier foundation figures showed 19,500 students had pledged to take part, with participating schools reporting a 12% increase in reading scores.That work has also brought Mahomes directly into Kansas City schools. In 2023, nearly 2,400 elementary students from 16 schools attended a Read for 15 rally where Mahomes spoke about the value of reading outside the classroom.The foundation has also used its platform to support youth beyond classrooms. Its programs have included youth volunteering, sports opportunities, food support and grants for community groups. In 2024, for example, the foundation partnered with Pete’s Garden on Kids Feeding Kids, a program involving culinary students preparing meals for families facing food insecurity.For the 2024-25 school year, more than 2,500 students were involved in that program and helped prepare and distribute more than 20,000 meals. That gives the foundation’s work another layer beyond direct donations: young people are also being encouraged to take part in helping their own communities.The foundation has also supported other causes connected to children and families, including education, athletics, children’s health, disability services and food access.What did Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes build in Kansas CityOne of the foundation’s clearest physical projects can be found at Martin Luther King Jr. Square Park in Kansas City.The 15 and the Mahomies Foundation gave $1 million toward the transformation of the park, helping create an inclusive playground designed for children with different physical and mental abilities. The project was developed with Kansas City Parks and Recreation and opened in August 2021.The playground includes accessible play equipment and sensory features, giving children with different needs a place where they can play together. The project also incorporated elements connected to Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s legacy.When the playground opened, Patrick Mahomes kept his message simple: “This is y’all’s park,” he told the crowd. “This is just the beginning for Kansas City’s future and the future of the kids in Kansas City, hopefully it will keep going.”The foundation’s support has also reached local charities through its annual gala. At its fifth annual gala in 2024, more than 850 supporters attended and $1.077 million was granted to 20 Kansas City charities.Brittany Mahomes later shared her reaction to the event, writing, “Truly a blessing to be able to make an impact in these communities!”Where else has the Mahomes foundation directed its moneyThe gala continues a pattern that began with the foundation’s first major event in 2019. That night, more than $600,000 was raised, while 15 Kansas City-area charities received $15,000 grants each through the foundation’s 15 for 15 program.The foundation has since expanded its list of causes. It has supported groups working in education, athletics, children’s health, disability services, food access, literacy and community support.Its work has also moved into food allergy awareness. In 2024, the foundation partnered with Food Allergy Research & Education on the 15 and FARE initiative in Kansas City. The program is aimed at improving access to food allergy resources and training for restaurants, schools and community food banks.Taken together, the numbers show that the Mahomes family’s charitable work is not limited to one large donation. The $1.625 million Boys & Girls Clubs commitment, $1 million playground contribution, literacy program and local charity grants have created several different ways for the foundation to reach children and families.For Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, much of that work is tied to places that shaped their own lives. Kansas City became Patrick’s professional home, while Texas remains closely connected to both of them. Their foundation has used those links to direct money and programs toward children, schools, clubs and community groups in those areas.The football career may be what made Patrick Mahomes a household name, but the foundation’s work gives his name a presence far beyond the NFL. More than 20,000 students have taken part in Read for 15, while other programs have provided meals, grants, youth opportunities and accessible spaces. articles.title: Is Madison Beer banned from attending Chargers games? Justin Herbert’s fiancée caught in viral NFL controversy
articles.summary: Last month, a viral claim sparked questions about whether Madison Beer had been banned from attending Los Angeles Chargers games after Justin Herbert
articles.body: Last month, a viral claim sparked questions about whether Madison Beer had been banned from attending Los Angeles Chargers games after Justin Herbert struggled on the field. The post alleged that head coach Jim Harbaugh had labelled Herbert’s fiancée a distraction and barred her from games and practices. However, the claim was not supported by any credible evidence. The account behind the post identified itself as a satire NFL page, making the supposed ban a joke rather than a real Chargers decision.Madison Beer was not banned from Chargers gamesThe claim surfaced on social media after the Chargers opened the 2026 season with two home defeats. Beer had attended both games at SoFi Stadium, where she was seen supporting Herbert from the stands.The viral post claimed Harbaugh had “banned” Beer from all Chargers games and team practices until further notice. It also suggested that the coach wanted Herbert to remain more focused for the rest of the season.There was no credible report confirming either claim. Harbaugh did not announce any such restriction during his media availability after the Chargers lost to the Las Vegas Raiders.More importantly, the account that posted the claim described itself as a “Satire NFL” account in its bio. That detail was central to the fact check and showed that the post was presented as parody rather than genuine reporting.Madison Beer’s presence drew attention amid Justin Herbert strugglesBeer’s appearances became a talking point because Herbert and the Chargers struggled during their first two home games. Los Angeles lost both matchups by identical 26-14 scores, first against the Arizona Cardinals and then against the Raiders.Herbert completed 15 of 27 passes for 192 yards against Las Vegas. He also threw two interceptions and fumbled three times, although the Chargers recovered each fumble.Some fans on social media began linking Beer’s presence to Herbert’s performances. However, those reactions were based on fan speculation rather than any statement from the Chargers or evidence connecting Beer to the quarterback’s struggles.The timing also gave the rumour extra attention. Beer and Herbert’s relationship has attracted interest beyond football, so her regular appearances at Chargers games naturally became part of the wider conversation surrounding the quarterback.As of last month, there was no indication that Beer had been barred from attending Chargers games, practices or supporting Herbert.The fact check served as a reminder that viral sports posts can quickly blur the line between satire and genuine reporting. articles.body: Fall has arrived in the Mahomes household, and Brittany Mahomes is making sure her three children get to enjoy every bit of it. Patrick carried Sterling on his shoulders while holding Golden Raye, while Bronze stayed close to his father. Brittany joined them in a Kansas City Chiefs shirt, sunglasses and rain boots.The children also appeared to enjoy a visit to Johnson Farms, where the fall setting gave them plenty to explore. articles.title: NFL's biggest surprises, disappointments and MVP through first 4 weeks of season
articles.summary: After four games, our NFL writers call out which teams and players are catching their attention for good and bad reasons, and could a running back really win...
articles.body:
Four weeks into the 2026 NFL season has provided fans early data points, tight ballgames , testy referees and the usual dollop of gripes about coaches and coordinators.

So which teams, players and coaches stood out? And what should we look forward to over the next set of games before we hit the NFL's midway point?

Yahoo Sports' Frank Schwab , Eric Edholm , Jay Busbee and Jori Epstein each weighed in with their takes on the NFL's top surprises, disappointments, MVPs and storylines.

Frank Schwab: Last season, the Raiders were an absolute mess with no plan and no hope for the future. That changed quickly. Las Vegas is coming off a loss Sunday, but even that was a competitive game against the Chiefs. The 3-1 start looks like it is sustainable, with a defense that is much improved and an offense that is revamped with rookie head coach Klint Kubiak.

The Raiders earned the No. 1 overall pick last season by being a horrendous team. This season, they should be a playoff contender. What a change.

Eric Edholm: The Raiders, and specifically the Klint Kubiak-Kirk Cousins duo, have been a highly competitive team. They started 3-0 before falling to the Chiefs at home, but they gave Kansas City everything it could handle and might be far more competitive than we realized. Cousins has thrown multiple TDs in every game despite missing Brock Bowers for two of them. This has completely taken the pressure off the Raiders to force rookie Fernando Mendoza into the lineup as a savior. Now they can develop him at a proper pace and hand over the baton when Mendoza is ready, not when a struggling team needs a boost. This short-term development could have important long-term benefits.

Jay Busbee: Since I'm writing this on Tuesday morning, I have to go with the Atlanta Falcons. After an opening two games in which the team didn't look capable of making the College Football Playoff, much less winning four games in the NFL, the Falcons are a completely new and revitalized team with Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback. How long will this run last? Who knows, but watching Bijan Robinson in open space is like watching poetry in motion … if poetry could run right over you.

Jori Epstein: Maybe it sounds silly to say the reigning Super Bowl MVP is a pleasant surprise. But Kenneth Walker III's 161 yards from scrimmage on the biggest stage did not represent his season-long average during four Seahawks years and certainly didn't represent his first four games of production in prior seasons. In no four-game start prior did Walker average more than 70.8 rushing yards and 85 yards from scrimmage per game. This year: He's riding a league-best 134.3 rushing yards and 155.3 yards from scrimmage through four weeks. His six touchdowns from scrimmage already surpass his five across 17 games last season. Credit Walker for his toughness, head coach Andy Reid for his creative play-calling, Patrick Mahomes for his general magician tendencies and the Chiefs' offensive line for paving the way even without their starting left tackle.

What I want to know next: Can Walker sustain this pace, or anything near it, over the course of a whole season?

Schwab: It seems too easy to say the Chargers, so I'll go to the AFC South and take the Texans. It's not just the 0-4 record, either. Houston's offense has been middling, and it fell apart without Nico Collins for a couple weeks. That isn't a huge surprise. What's surprising is the Texans' defense hasn't been very good. Needing a stop in Week 4 to get their first win, the Texans allowed Dak Prescott to drive downfield. They gave up 17 catches and 189 yards to CeeDee Lamb. This is supposed to be a great defense and it's not even that good. That's stunning.

Edholm: It's gotta be the Texans, who dropped another game late Sunday — and another game at home, too. That's 0-4 overall, and 0-3 in Houston. They battled back from the 0-3 start a year ago, but this hill is an even higher climb. More than anything, how they're losing is the most bothersome aspect. The defense was unglued in losses to the Bills and Cowboys. Granted, those are two of the league's better offenses, but this Texans' defense entered the season regarded as elite; that hasn't been the case so far. QB C.J. Stroud hasn't turned the ball over the past three games, but he's still missing some throws and being sacked too often. We'll see if this team can pull out of this tailspin, but it's not looking great early.

Busbee: Well, Frank left the Chargers sitting right there for me like an Easter egg on the middle of the lawn, so I'll grab them. Everything about Los Angeles seemed to be pointing toward a deep January run prior to this season, and everything now points to a six-win ceiling. Injuries, incompetence, and an inability for Justin Herbert and new OC Mike McDaniel to connect have all contributed to a dismal 0-4 start to a season that could still get so much worse.

Epstein: The Los Angeles Chargers' offense.

I wasn't sure the Chargers would be great this year. But I did believe one of Mike McDaniel's key offensive principles would help Justin Herbert improve this season.

McDaniel told me when I visited Chargers training camp how he believed NFL pass rushers are on average better than NFL offensive linemen. "So if you accept the fact that blockers have an inherent disadvantage," he said, "to me, beating the pass rush with the time of the play more often than not is where those beliefs come from." McDaniel in turn wanted Herbert to focus on quick-release passes, a strategy that should leave him less reliant on a seemingly always injured offensive line and less susceptible to excessive hits. Yards after the catch was to be the name of the game. Instead: Herbert's 12 sacks trail only Aaron Rodgers and Baker Mayfield; the 35 pressures he's faced trail only Rodgers, the Panthers' Bryce Young and the Packers' Jordan Love.

Herbert's six interceptions to four passing touchdowns have tanked his passer rating to a 70.6, 31st out of 32 quarterbacks who have attempted at least 50 passes (Jameis Winston trails slightly, at 70.4). And the Chargers, in the "most important" stat, are 0-4. Their schedule remains daunting and questions linger about their offensive identity. Injuries, particularly to the offensive line, contribute heavily. And the Chargers lost to the Bills and Seahawks by one score. So there's reason to believe they can turn the corner. But through four games, they're disappointing.

Schwab: It's always fun when a non-quarterback is in the race for MVP, even though we all know that a quarterback will win the award. But who has had more value so far this season than Kenneth Walker? He has transformed the Chiefs' offense, and KC is 4-0 after a hugely disappointing 6-11 season in 2025. He already has 537 rushing yards and is averaging 6.2 yards per carry, and both marks lead the NFL.

MVP has become a quarterback-only award. But it would be nice if Walker at least stayed in the conversation because no one player has had a bigger impact this season.

Edholm: Brock Purdy has played elite football and is on pace for his finest season, statistically and otherwise, to date. Why he doesn't receive proper credit is beyond me, but Purdy needs recognition for his growth and efficiency, especially with the 49ers again being ravaged by injuries on both sides of the ball. He hasn't been sacked all season, and Purdy is completing nearly 70% of his passes and averaging 8.9 yards per attempt despite multiple receivers being hurt early in the season. And no one asked, but my OPOY is Kenneth Walker.

Busbee: I'm going with Kirk Cousins because uprooting your life and taking on a role that you know has a ticking clock is one thing; excelling in that role against all logical and roster-based odds is another. Cousins has thrown 11 touchdowns, tied with Brock Purdy for the league lead, but unlike Purdy, Cousins is doing this with a team that's already more than halfway to its preseason over/under of 5.5 wins. Is it sustainable? Probably not, but the Kirko Express is a fun ride for now.

Epstein: I'm torn between San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy and Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen, who have led their teams to 4-0 and 3-1 starts, respectively. Purdy's 11 passing touchdowns tie the Raiders' Kirk Cousins for most through four weeks, Purdy's 126.2 passer rating and 61.9% success rate (another efficiency metric) are best in the league. Two of those wins have come against the Los Angeles Rams and Denver Broncos, who played in conference championship games last season. And Purdy has played while down a host of receivers, which should neutralize questions about whether he's simply capitalizing on injured (and, in Week 1, highly jetlagged) competition. That said, Allen has 13 total touchdowns (six passing, seven rushing) and remains a dual threat teams fear facing. He's thrown three picks the last two weeks, which gives cause for concern, but his dual-threat style may nonetheless still instill more fear in opponents than any of his counterparts right now.

To break the tie, I'll fall back on the criteria I've long used to discern between the best players and the most valuable players: Who has provided the most value to their team, based on the combination of what they've been asked to and what they've done? Through four weeks, Purdy gets the nod.

What's the top storyline to watch in the next four weeks?

Schwab: The Jaguars are one bad half at Denver from already being the story of the NFL through four games. They went 13-4 last season and look great during a 3-1 start to this season. But because Jacksonville struggles to get attention and the Jaguars did blow that game at the Broncos in Week 2, they're still well under the radar. But this looks like a complete team that can win a Super Bowl. There is practically no competition for the Jags in the AFC South (the other three teams are a combined 2-10). It will take too long for anyone to notice, but perhaps in the next quarter of the season everyone will realize the Jaguars are one of the NFL's elite teams.

Edholm: I'm looking at the NFC West race. Week 5 brings us a great matchup: the 4-0 49ers at the 3-1 Seahawks, and it's a critical stretch for both. The Seahawks have three of their next four games at home, but they face a tough quartet of teams. After facing the Seahawks, the 49ers play the Commanders (with Jayden Daniels potentially back) and the suddenly hot Falcons in Atlanta, followed by the Week 8 bye. And lest we forget about the Rams, who are 2-2 (barely) and also enjoy three of their next four games at home, although the next one is against a Bills team coming off a loss. The league's tightest division is entering a key stage of the season.

Busbee: I'm going to be interested to see if anyone can take control of the NFC East, which seems like the most up-for-grabs division in football right now. Seriously, you could make a case for any of the four teams to win it — a case largely based on the fact that all of the four teams have a tendency to underachieve at spectacularly awful levels. I still think Dallas has the horses to pull this one out, but given the high variance at play here, no winner would surprise me that much.

Epstein: Can Kyler Murray and the Vikings' offense figure things out? Clearly Minnesota's defense is playoff-caliber. The Vikings are 4-0 on the backs of a unit allowing fewer points than any other team in the NFL. But can Murray, who previously operated less in the pocket than head coach Kevin O'Connell's quarterbacks historically have, mesh well in this offense? How much of a shaky start reflects the injuries to players, including star receiver Justin Jefferson, how much reflects a standard acclimation period and how much reflects a player whose style differs from the Sam Darnold/Kirk Cousins type that O'Connell has thrived with? Murray was more efficient against the Miami Dolphins than he was against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but I want to know how Murray competes against playoff-caliber teams rather than the 0-4 units he's faced the last two weeks. If O'Connell, Murray and Co. settle the offense, the Vikings have the chance to threaten any team in the league.

articles.title: NFL Trade Rumor: $29M Arizona Cardinals WR could help Justin Herbert’s Los Angeles Chargers save their 2026 season
articles.summary: The Justin Herbert-led Los Angeles Chargers began their 2026 campaign with one goal: doing more than what they did in 2025.
articles.body: The Justin Herbert-led Los Angeles Chargers began their 2026 campaign with one goal: doing more than what they did in 2025. But their 0-4 start has tormented that very goal.With the trade deadline approaching faster than ever [Nov. 10], adding a proven playmaker could help the Chargers save their 2026 NFL season. One interesting candidate comes via the Arizona Cardinals: Marvin Harrison Jr.Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay suggests the 24-year-old Ohio State self-repped Maserati Marv as a trade candidate for Los Angeles. All that Arizona has to do is send their 2027 third-round pick to acquire the No. 4 overall selection.Marvin Harrison Jr trade rumors link Arizona WR to Chiefs and ChargersAccording to Yahoo Sports Daily host Coley Harvey, Marvin Harrison Jr. needs to be with a contender.He came out of Ohio State. He was used to winning and being in the college football playoff, along with big primetime moments. He’s missing that edge, that added competition to get his competitive juices going.Yahoo Sports Daily host Coley Harvey had paired Harrison with the Kansas City Chiefs. But the Los Angeles Chargers, who finished second in the AFC West division in 2025, were also viewed as an almost-contending team.They were expected to turn things around in 2026 - especially after signing Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel, under whom Tyreek Hill shone.But nothing of that sort happened in Los Angeles. Everybody’s in shock. And so, everybody’s pairing whoever seems like a misfit on another team with the Chargers.In the current scenario, it looks like a Maserati Marv! Now where does Marvin Harrison Jr. fit into Justin Herbert’s puzzle? Let’s find that out.Why Marvin Harrison Jr is perfect for Los AngelesThe Los Angeles Chargers are suffering, despite bringing in Mike McDaniel from Miami. Their offense has struggled so badly that it ranks 29th in scoring, at 16.8 points per game, and averages only 185 passing yards per game through the first four weeks.Injuries to Ladd McConkey [foot] and Rashawn Slater [high ankle sprain] have also complicated the Chargers’ offensive cruise. In moments like these, only a new member can help.For instance, Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., someone who desperately needs a new environment. Though his numbers could explain the itch everybody’s feeling before plunging to sign him.Harrison recorded 62 catches for 885 yards and 8 touchdowns as a rookie in 2024. His Year 2 showed a different side: 41 receptions for 608 yards and 4 touchdowns.His year 3 is trending toward a depreciating value, with just 5 receptions for 85 yards and 1 touchdown in 4 games. If it continues, he could record less than what he did in 2025. All he needs is a change of scenery.Kyler Murray vs Jacoby BrissettKyler Murray played in all 17 games in 2024 and just 5 games in 2025, with Jacoby Brissett playing the remainder of that season. That is where Marvin Harrison Jr. struggled.Harrison excelled in 2024 when Murray was playing, but his production dropped drastically with Brissett, partly due to various injuries like a foot/heel issue, appendicitis, and a concussion.Harrison returned in 2026 to play under Brissett once more, though it looks like Brissett may not be the right fit for him - or perhaps the quarterback has already found a favorite target.Whatever the reason, if any franchise, particularly the Los Angeles Chargers, decides to trade for Harrison, it will require a significant financial commitment.Marvin Harrison contract detailsHe signed a rookie contract worth $35 million. His career earnings through 2026 are $29 million. His 2026 salary cap charge is approx. $9 million.He carries a $23 million dead cap value. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $325 million KC Current stadium expansion gets green light with $185 million funding
articles.summary: The Kansas City Current are preparing for a much bigger future at CPKC Stadium, and the latest move could reshape the club’s place in women’s soccer.
articles.body: The Kansas City Current are preparing for a much bigger future at CPKC Stadium, and the latest move could reshape the club’s place in women’s soccer. Kansas City has approved $185 million in public funding for the stadium expansion, paving the way for thousands of new seats and major improvements around the Riverfront. For co-owners Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, the project adds another major chapter to a club they have helped build from the ground up. The expansion also strengthens Kansas City’s bid to attract major international sporting events and turn the Riverfront into an even bigger destination for fans.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current investment growsThe Mahomes connection to the Kansas City Current goes beyond Patrick’s profile as the Chiefs’ star quarterback. Brittany Mahomes was part of the original ownership group that brought the NWSL franchise to Kansas City, while Patrick joined the ownership team in 2023. The Current officially lists both as co-owners, alongside Angie Long and Chris Long.That gives the stadium expansion added significance for the Mahomes family. CPKC Stadium opened in 2024 with 11,500 seats and quickly became a major symbol of the growth of women’s professional sports. Now, the proposed work would increase capacity to 18,000.The plan calls for about 6,500 additional seats, mainly in the corners between the existing grandstands. The club also intends to raise the roofline, add more premium boxes and double its suite capacity.For a team that has already attracted strong crowds, the larger venue could give the Current more room to build its audience while creating additional opportunities for premium hospitality and major events.CPKC Stadium expansion could transform Kansas City’s RiverfrontThe stadium project is part of a much larger transformation of the Berkley Riverfront area. The broader $1.4 billion development is expected to bring new housing, retail, parking and infrastructure improvements, creating a district designed to remain active beyond match days.The Current also sees the expanded stadium as a potential gateway to major international events. Kansas City is looking ahead to opportunities such as the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup and the Men’s Rugby World Cup, making venue capacity and facilities increasingly important.There is also a financial safeguard attached to the public funding. The team and its development partners have committed to covering the city’s bond debt if tax revenue does not generate enough money to meet those payments.Construction on the stadium expansion is expected to begin after next season. AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

With the calendar flipped to October, and as weather cools and the days get shorter, it's a sure sign we need to take a big-picture look at the NFL landscape.

We've reached the end of the first quarter of the 2026 season (four games into a 17-game season, so close enough), and that means it's time to assign grades to all 32 teams.

These grades factor in a combination of game results, preseason expectations, a deeper dive into stats, injuries and projections going forward. Here's how the Yahoo Sports NFL staff assessed every team, with Frank Schwab grading the AFC teams and Eric Edholm evaluating the NFC.

The Bills were close to getting an A. All they had to do was beat the Patriots at home, and they would have been 4-0 with a three-game lead in the division. They had a 26-21 lead at the two-minute warning. They lost and while it's harsh to dock them a full grade for losing a close game to a team that went 14-3 last season, it was a lost opportunity. And suddenly a defense that is 27th in yardage allowed looks shaky. That needs to be fixed.

Losing on the road to the Seahawks and Jaguars isn't too bad. That's what happens when the schedule gets tougher. The way the Patriots have looked in those games is what sets the grade back. Drake Maye had three poor games before playing well in a huge spot at the Bills in Week 4. That helped. The offense as a whole still has to find consistency. A 2-2 start isn't the end of the world, but it's hard to give the Patriots better than an average grade.

When your only win is against the Titans, it's hard to get too excited. The Jets have shown progress. They were in games late against the Packers and Lions. They even have an interception, which they failed to do all of last season. This isn't the same horrendous team from a season ago. It's not good one either. The lopsided loss to the Bears, who were on their third starting quarterback of the season, was not a good sign. There have been more positive signs than last season, but that's not saying too much.

The Dolphins have been outscored 101-46 in four games. They have lost by double digits in three of them. They're the second team in 22 years to fail to score 14 points in any of their first four games (the other one was the 2019 Dolphins). Malik Willis hasn't played well, though it's hard to blame him considering the situation around him. De'Von Achane, the one star on the roster, is out for the season. So why not an F? This team wasn't expected to be good, and at least some rookies, like linebacker Jacob Rodriguez and receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, have had some moments. The biggest goal now is getting that first win to avoid 0-17 questions.

A blown lead in the second half against the Saints ruined a perfect 4-0 start. And the Ravens bogged down in the second half against a terrible Titans team in Week 4, squeaking out a win with Lamar Jackson sitting after halftime with an ankle injury. It would be nice to see Jackson and wideout Zay Flowers both healthy for more than a half at a time because the short glimpses of that have been great. When Flowers and Jackson played the first halves against the Colts and Titans before injuries, the combined score was 55-20. It still seems tenuous because the Ravens' stars can't stay healthy.

Through two weeks the Bengals were undefeated and their defense looked very good. Then that unit was smashed by the Steelers in Week 3. Cincinnati followed that up with a home loss to Jacksonville. The defense has been above average on the whole, which provides a path for the Bengals to be an AFC North contender and maybe more. Now that the Bengals have their annual mediocre start out of the way, we can see if they can elevate to a higher level.

There are reasons to be skeptical. A team can't live off close wins in the final minutes, and in all three Browns wins they've grabbed the lead in the final four minutes. Cleveland's offense is still up and down, and the idea that Deshaun Watson is playing very well is overblown. Still, what more could Cleveland have wanted than a 3-1 record? New head coach Todd Monken has done a good job, and many young players are playing well and offering a bright future. The Browns are unlikely to maintain a winning record for much longer unless the offense finds more consistency, but it has been a great start to the season.

A win against the Bengals was pretty good. The rest has been shaky. Pittsburgh struggled to put away an Atlanta team with Cooper Rush at quarterback, lost 20-3 to New England and let Deshaun Watson have his best game for Cleveland in a prime-time road loss. The Steelers' defense looks old and while 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers is playing well for his age, it's still not a dynamic offense. There's very little upside to the Steelers, and that's been the case for a few years.

The Jaguars have looked like one of the best teams in the NFL for seven of the eight quarters they have played. Letting the Broncos come back and win in Week 2 cost them an A+ start to the season. The Jaguars are strong on offense and defense, which shouldn't be a surprise because they were a complete team last season as well. Trevor Lawrence has a 111.2 passer rating. He has never been above 100 over a full season. The AFC South isn't providing much competition. Jacksonville could have the division clinched by early December.

Any hope that the Colts would replicate their offensive magic from the first half of last season with Daniel Jones back in the lineup has dwindled. Jones, coming off an Achilles injury, has been below average. Things might look better if the Colts' first two games weren't against the Ravens and Chiefs. And the Colts did take the Chiefs, who are now 4-0, to overtime at Arrowhead. Indy's defense has gotten better the past couple weeks after a rough start. The Colts' offense still has Jonathan Taylor. At 2-2, the Colts can improve and have a successful season.

The only positive is that the Texans are maybe better than they seem but unlucky in close games. Three of their losses came by no more than five points. They led in the final two minutes of all three of those losses. But 0-4 is 0-4. Nobody is giving out a consolation prize for coming close over and over. The Texans can't finish, which is an indictment of a defense that was supposed to be elite but has been closer to average. The Texans might not be bad but they're in a deep hole and that's a massive disappointment.

The Titans signed over $333 million in free-agent deals in the offseason, the most in the NFL, according to Spotrac . They hired a brand new coaching staff led by Robert Saleh. They had three top-60 draft picks, including two in the first round. And what has changed? The Titans would be the worst team in the NFL if it weren't for the Dolphins. You have to squint hard to see any progress from second-year quarterback Cam Ward. Their last three losses have all been by one score, so maybe they're closing in on a win and a breakthrough after that. But it has been an ugly start to what was supposed to be an improved era.

Let's not forget the Chiefs went 6-11, including 6-8 in Patrick Mahomes' starts, and Mahomes was coming off an ACL suffered last December. Starting the season 4-0 was far from guaranteed. But Kenneth Walker III has been perhaps the most impactful player in the NFL through four games, Mahomes looks healthy and the Chiefs seem to have gotten their dynasty back on track. Maybe injuries on offense catch up to them and it starts to go south, but that's a problem for down the road. Right now the start for the Chiefs couldn't be much better.

It's hard to bash a team that has wins over the Rams and Jaguars too much. But any honest Broncos fan would admit there are serious concerns. Denver needed second-half rallies to beat LA and Jacksonville, which might speak to its home-field altitude advantage in September more than how well the Broncos are playing. Their offense has mostly been awful with coordinator Davis Webb calling plays. The run and pass games have lagged behind. New star receiver Jaylen Waddle has been a non-factor in three of four games, which is hard to believe. Denver's defense hasn't been terrible, but it's also difficult to shake the image of players missing tackle after tackle in the opener at Kansas City. Two quality wins aside, there's a lot of improvement that needs to be made.

Sure, a win over the Chiefs would have been nice. But that shouldn't dampen a great start from a Raiders team that had sunk to the bottom of the NFL last season. Klint Kubiak looks like a very good hire as head coach. His offensive scheme has led to immediate results. Free-agent additions have already paid off, especially with a defense that has improved tremendously. For a franchise that has been wretched for decades, the first four games of this season have been a revelation. The Raiders don't look like they're going away anytime soon.

We'd give the Chargers a lower grade if possible. How are they this bad? How does Justin Herbert look like one of the NFL's worst quarterbacks? Losing defensive coordinator Jesse Minter was always going to have an impact, but new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was supposed to offset that. Instead, Jim Harbaugh is already being asked about firing McDaniel. It's not the wildest idea after McDaniel's offense has looked consistently out of sync and nowhere near accommodating his players' strengths. The Chargers started the season by losing two home games as a big favorite in each one, then somehow lost a game at Buffalo in which they were +4 in turnover margin and fell behind 27-6 to Seattle. A team that was 11-6 last season looks barely a step above an expansion team. Only Miami has a worse DVOA; even the Titans rank ahead of the Chargers there. It's unfathomable.

Sunday's dramatic victory at the Texans probably raised this from a C, or a C-. That and the Joey Porter Jr. trade . The landscape is there for Dallas to make a move in the East. Two division foes are missing their starting quarterbacks, and the other one is slumping. Dak Prescott is off to a strong start again, and the offense is starting to get hot. The problem has been the defense, which has yet to mature. Can Porter help unlock the group? With this offense, the Cowboys need only one or two more stops per game.

They're first in the NFC East, which is something they've rarely been able to say recently, and John Harbaugh has them winning games they need. That's the good news. The bad is the Jaxson Dart injury caps this grade until we see evidence that the Giants' replacement-QB floor is anywhere close to where Dart was. Losing Brian Burns is also crushing, even if New York's defense keeps making plays.

Amid high expectations, the Eagles have come out flat — two shaky wins against lesser clubs followed by two disappointing losses to two better conference foes. Losing by 20 to the Case Keenum-led Bears was humiliating and blowing a late 10-point lead at home to the Rams was downright demoralizing. They've also been gutted by injuries, with DeVonta Smith, Lane Johnson and Zack Baun all missing Sunday, and Saquon Barkley, Quinyon Mitchell and Jonathan Greenard were all injured during the Rams loss. Jalen Hurts and his offense are again struggling, and it's not an overnight fix.

The Commanders can claim one of the better results of the 2026 season, handing the defending champion Seahawks their only loss so far. A close defeat to the Eagles is fine, but two 17-point losses — and two notable QB injuries — reveal a tough picture again in Washington. Jayden Daniels isn't expected to go on injured reserve, but the recurrence rate of his left elbow injury has to be very concerning, especially with backup Marcus Mariota getting hurt in London. Washington is 0-2 in the division and has the third-worst point differential in the league. This is the reality. If Daniels can return and the Commanders can beat the Giants, the grade would flip dramatically.

They have won two straight without Caleb Williams, which is a significant development. Williams' Grade 2 hamstring strain is likely to keep him sidelined a bit longer, but Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent have held down the fort well in two home games, even with Bagent having three picks wiped out by penalty against the Jets . Ben Johnson's offensive innovation has been on display, boasting a strong running game with Williams out. The home loss to the unbeaten Vikings stings but the Bears have played strong defense after allowing 37 points to Carolina in Week 1. It has been an imperfect start, but a mostly encouraging one.

This Lions' offense can match firepower with just about anyone. But the state of Detroit's defense is far less encouraging, allowing a league-worst 3.0 points per drive . They've been outscored on the season and are fortunate to be 2-2. They easily could have lost at home to the Saints in Week 1 and needed late plays to hold off the Jets in Detroit. This isn't a winning formula; it's a get-by-and-survive one. The Lions have an early bye after heading to Arizona this weekend, and they clearly must find solutions on the defensive side to be taken seriously as contenders. They can still win the North, but the intimidation factor with facing this team has dissipated. Opponents know they can score against them early and often.

The product has looked to be about a D+, especially when you consider the team's injuries. On the other hand, the Packers are still 2-2 with three of their next four games at Lambeau Field. They're hanging around in the division. There's hope with Micah Parsons' imminent return, but the injury/suspension situation on offense doesn't bode well, with right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele and receiver Jayden Reed out for the season, and RB Josh Jacobs remaining on the commissioner's exempt list. The Edgerrin Cooper injury in Week 4 also is a big blow . The Packers could use a convincing victory against a quality foe, with a great opportunity against the Bears on Sunday. Jordan Love is being paid like a top-tier quarterback, so somehow he and head coach Matt LaFleur must pick up the pace — and likely do so without a dependable run game.

There's not much to gripe about this undefeated record, but the Vikings clearly have some limitations. They put away the Bears, Bucs and Dolphins the past three games, yet with difficulty. The problem is an offense that has averaged 15.7 ppg the past three weeks, with Kyler Murray not yet finding his rhythm after missing nearly two full games with a concussion. Injuries to star wideout Justin Jefferson, and offensive linemen Christian Darrisaw and Donovan Jackson have also put a damper on things. Murray and Jefferson have played only 18 snaps together so far. Minnesota's defense has been hellacious to start the season, but the offense must pick up the pace. An A grade is achievable, but they're not there yet.

It's hard not to wonder what this team might have looked like had Michael Penix Jr. been healthy for Week 1. After two absolute stinkers offensively, the Falcons have looked extremely dangerous the past two games, raising the floor and the ceiling of the entire operation. They blowtorched the Saints on Monday in what was supposed to be the Saints' emotional evening. Atlanta's defense has also played pretty well on the whole, especially against the run. This team's arc has completely changed, and while the grade factors in the record, it also reflects the major upward swing, suggesting this team could be a sneaky problem.

Carolina is sitting atop the division at its bye week, but the Panthers' profile is lopsided; things would have looked different had they not blown a lead against the Browns. The offense has been the story, with Bryce Young leading the NFL in passing yards and Tetairoa McMillan playing like an elite receiver, especially against the Lions with Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette out. The Panthers' defense has rallied since the 59-point bloodletting against the Bears, but there's a question of whether that unit can take care of business against some of the other better offenses around the NFL. We'll keep our eyes on injuries to rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling (knee) and linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), but Carolina has legit division-title hopes again with the NFC South still profiling as a weaker crop.

The narrow loss at Detroit and the stunning win in Baltimore had this team thinking big things, especially in a typically volatile NFC South. But the wheels have come off in two home games, where the Saints blew a fourth-quarter lead against the Raiders and completely no-showed Monday night against the Falcons. New Orleans' run defense was poor entering the Atlanta game, and the Falcons shredded through them with ease. QB Tyler Shough also has hit a small wall in his second season, even if he's hardly the biggest issue. Injuries, like running back Travis Etienne Jr.'s hamstring ailment, have taken a bite out of the Saints, and though they're only a game behind the 2-2 Falcons and Panthers, it feels like New Orleans needs a change in mojo after the past few games.

An F grade might not have been out of bounds, but there have been mitigating factors to the winless start. All four losses have been one-score games, and Baker Mayfield's thumb injury has been a tough blow the Bucs will have to weather. Mayfield wasn't playing great prior to his injury, and the Bucs have been giving up an average of four sacks per game. The defense has been decent enough, even with injuries. And though this doesn't look like one of the worst teams in the league, the record is what it is. Head coach Todd Bowles and offensive coordinator Zac Robinson are catching heat, and there might not be any truly easy games prior to the Week 10 bye.

Mike LaFleur's Week 1 win over the Chargers felt like the Cardinals might be due for a reevaluation. But three straight losses have shown us just how far Arizona needs to come. The offense has flip-flopped between competent and bad every other week. The defense has not been able to pick up the slack either, although you can hardly blame the Giants loss on that unit. In that game, Jacoby Brissett threw two picks before Arizona's final drive. Yet LaFleur called four straight passes inside the 4-yard line, with the final play resulting in a game-sealing pick 6. Why did the Cardinals draft running back Jeremiyah Love third overall? Maybe things improve with a QB change, but the defensive limitations are likely too big to overcome.

For a team some were brave enough to bestow 17-0 predictions on , the Rams have looked pretty darned ordinary. They were staring 1-3 in the face prior to the tremendous fourth-quarter comeback in Philadelphia. Aaron Donald missed that one, Puka Nacua missed time and Myles Garrett remains out, so there's a health factor baked in here. The Rams have also been more December-January teams in Sean McVay's history, getting off to some slow starts in multiple playoff years. But Matthew Stafford's turnovers are hurting them, especially in the loss to the Broncos when the Rams blew a 16-0 lead. Stafford's two picks nearly sank them against the Eagles. LA's defense has mostly been strong since the Australia game, but the offense and special teams are holding the team back, in spite of some beefy yardage totals.

They're the only unbeaten team in the thorny NFC West, and as usual, the Niners had to endure a lengthy list of injuries. Despite that, their offense has been terrific, and their defense has been mostly sharp, outside of the shootout against the Cardinals. Still, it's hard to gripe about what we've seen, especially from Brock Purdy's tremendous start. He hasn't been sacked once in four games and is on pace for his best statistical season by a mile. The trip to Seattle will be the Niners' biggest gut check to date, but this team appears legitimate. Grade: A

The Sam Darnold injury ended up being a blessing, far less serious than it could have been, and Drew Lock held down the fort effectively. The loss at Washington in Darnold's return is probably the only thing keeping this grade from being in the A range, even if the Seahawks let teams hang around a bit too often. Even after dominating the Chargers for three quarters, they kept the backdoor open and let Justin Herbert make it interesting. The Seahawks remain one of the biggest threats, but the backfield health is a potential sore spot, and the late-game sloppiness needs to be tidied up.
